# Yetda

> Yetda (옜다, Korean for "here, take it") is a free, open-source macOS menu bar app that puts a screenshot straight into the prompt of a coding agent running in your terminal — Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, opencode, Cursor CLI and others. Tap ⌘ twice (or press ⌘⇧2), drag a region, and the image is pasted into the agent. API keys, tokens and passwords in the capture are masked on-device first.

Key facts:

- Platform: macOS 13 or later, Apple silicon and Intel. Signed with Developer ID and notarized by Apple.
- Install: `brew install --cask woonmayer/tap/yetda`, or download https://github.com/woonmayer/homebrew-tap/releases/latest/download/Yetda.dmg
- Price: free. License: MIT. Source: https://github.com/woonmayer/yetda
- Privacy: no network access and no analytics; OCR and secret detection run on the Mac. Captures are kept in `~/Yetda/` and deleted after 7 days.
- Permissions: Screen Recording (to capture) and Accessibility (to paste into the terminal and detect the ⌘⌘ tap). Yetda does not record what you type.
- Terminals: Terminal, iTerm2, Ghostty, Warp, WezTerm, kitty, Alacritty, Hyper and more; any other app can be added from the menu.
- Several screenshots at once: the bundled `/shots` skill for Claude Code and Codex feeds all pending captures into the session.
- Paste an earlier capture: ⌘⇧1 opens a thumbnail menu of the 10 newest captures.
